newsitem.title: CANADA: Concorde lands in Halifax after engine trouble.
newsitem.headline: Concorde lands in Halifax after engine trouble.

text.p: A British Airways Concorde jet en route to New York with 70 passengers and nine crew on board made an emergency landing in Halifax, Nova Scotia, on Friday after it developed engine trouble over the Atlantic, airport officials said.
The plane landed safely in the Canadian east coast city shortly before 10 A.M. EST (1500 GMT) on three of its four engines.
"The captain experienced a problem with number three engine and purely as a precautionary measure, he decided to divert to Halifax," British Airways spokeswoman Honour Verrier said.
She was unable to provide details on the nature of the engine problem. The jet landed without incident an no passengers were injured.
"We didn't have emergency crews out there. No assistance was required," the Halifax airport duty manager told Reuters.
The Concorde was travelling to New York's John F Kennedy airport from London.
Another Concorde leaving London for New York would be diverted to Halifax to pick up the passengers at about noon EST (1700 GMT) and take them to New York, Verrier said.
